questions: Should datetime objects be serialized with timezone information preserved (e.g., ISO format with +00:00) or converted to naive UTC/local string?
For numpy.ndarray, should nested arrays (multidimensional) be serialized recursively as lists, or flattened?
Should Decimal serialization as string use scientific notation for large/small numbers, or always decimal notation?
If a datetime object is nested inside a numpy array (e.g., object dtype), should it be serialized via the datetime handler or the array handler?
Should the custom encoder also handle subclasses of the supported types (e.g., a custom Decimal subclass)?
For unsupported types, does the fallback to default JSONEncoder include trying to serialize iterables or other standard types not explicitly listed?
Should the output JSON string have any formatting (indentation, separators) or be compact?
If a Decimal has trailing zeros (e.g., Decimal('10.00')), should str(obj) preserve them, or normalize?
